context: Confirm the todo-db >= 0.3 packaging and how the wrapper is expected to delegate (see .claude/skills/todo-db/SKILL.md rule 4 for wrappers), then wire it so 'todo update' works in-repo without the wrapper itself becoming a handler for it. Verify the TestSkillThinness disjointness tests still pass.
description: Amendment is already solved upstream: todo-db >= 0.3 ships an 'update' verb, declared machine-readably in the skill sidecar as standalone_only_commands and deliberately NOT implemented by this repo's embedded _project/scripts/todo_db.py wrapper. Two tests in tests/unit/scripts/test_todo_wrapper.py enforce that boundary (TestSkillThinness), one hardcoding 'update' as the example of a wrapper-unsupported verb. So the repo currently cannot amend an item at all: scope, verifications and descriptions stay create-time-only, and three separate instances of that biting were recorded in the 2026-07-25/26 batches -- four promoted items born with no scope or ladder, a verification rung that can never pass, and an item description recommending an approach research had disproved. Decide and implement the adoption path: either take todo-db >= 0.3 as a dependency and route _project/scripts/todo to it, or have the wrapper delegate specifically its unsupported verbs to the standalone CLI when installed. Either way keep the disjointness invariant the wrapper tests encode.

preserves.behavior: standalone_only_commands and wrapper handlers stay disjoint (TestSkillThinness)
